B4 ipv4-ranges.notes: BlockedV4 matches ListedV4 range for range, including 192.0.0.0/16 and 198.18/15; matches the old TS conditions. Witnesses: 8.8.8.8 admitted, 10.0.0.1 refused.

B6 ipv6-ranges.notes: The exact negation of BlockedV6; matches the old TS on normalized forms. Scope note: 6to4, Teredo and 3fff::/20 are admitted, as the old guard admitted them.

M6 ipv4-mapped.notes: The English matches the lemma for ::/96, ::ffff:0:0/96 and 64:ff9b::/96 whatever IPv4 they embed; entailed by B6, kept as a named security statement.

P1 prune.notes: LiveRevSpec and RevOntoSpec give Elems(Recent) == FreshOf; same keep-set as the old timestamp > now - window filter. Witness: [0,500,1000] at 1000, window 1000 keeps [500,1000].

A1 admission.notes: Admitted iff fewer than maximum fresh attempts, keeping them followed by now; the old recent.length < maximum then push. Witness: empty with maximum 1 is admitted with [now].

S1 stale.notes: Corollary of A1 with NoneFresh; kills nothing alone, which is structural and acceptable.

W1 window.notes: Per admitted attempt, via KeptCounts and A1; the window consequence holds for non-decreasing time (Assumption A2), eviction covered by A2; kills nothing alone.

general: Shell matches the laws and the old TS on every normalized input enumerated. Residual scope notes for the maintainer: LRU eviction of a key that still has fresh attempts once 4,096 addresses are retained, which can reset its window (protocol.md promises an exact window over at most 4,096 LRU addresses); unchanged from the old code, whose !has(key) guard ran after delete(key) and was always true, and confirmed by the differential's identical retainedKeyCount; and 6to4/Teredo/3fff::/20 admission, as before.
